# SK2007 — The collection being enumerated is modified inside the loop

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A `foreach` over a `List<T>`, `Dictionary<,>` or `HashSet<T>` whose body adds to or removes from the same collection.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.2 |

## Why

The BCL collections carry a version counter, and `MoveNext` throws `InvalidOperationException` the moment it sees the version move. Because the loop the rule reports has no `break`, no `return` and no `throw`, the enumerator is guaranteed to be advanced at least once after the mutation — including past the last element, where `MoveNext` still runs to return `false`. So this is not a risk that a particular input might hit: it is a throw on every execution that reaches the mutation. The standard repair is to enumerate a snapshot, which is what the fix writes.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
foreach (var item in items) {
    if (item.Expired) {
        items.Remove(item);
    }
}
```

Write:

```csharp
foreach (var item in items.ToList()) {
    if (item.Expired) {
        items.Remove(item);
    }
}
```

## When it does not fire

Four guards, and each removes a way of being wrong rather than a way of being noisy. ⚠ **The collection type is matched against a closed list of BCL types whose enumerator is version-checked** — `List<T>`, `Dictionary<,>`, `HashSet<T>`, `SortedList<,>`, `SortedDictionary<,>`, `SortedSet<T>`, `Queue<T>`, `Stack<T>`, `Collection<T>` and `ObservableCollection<T>` — never against `ICollection<T>`, because a concurrent collection is *designed* to be modified while it is enumerated and a custom implementation may be too. ⚠ **The loop expression and the mutation's receiver must resolve to the same symbol**, so `foreach (var x in a) b.Remove(x)` is not this. ⚠ **A loop body containing any `break`, `return`, `throw` or `goto` that could leave this loop is skipped entirely**, because `items.Remove(item); break;` is the one legal spelling and the rule cannot prove which of several exits a path takes. Mutations inside a nested lambda or local function are ignored for the same reason: the rule cannot say when the delegate runs. ⚠ **The fix is offered only where `System.Linq` is already in scope**, since a repair whose text does not compile is worse than no repair; and it is marked unsafe, because enumerating a snapshot is a deliberate change to what the loop iterates, not a rewrite of the same program.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2007.severity`
